title.zh: 卷二十四 本紀第二十四 高宗一
title.raw: 卷二十四 本紀第二十四 高宗一 Volume 24 Annals 24: Gaozong 1

sentences.zh: 高宗受命中興全功至德聖神武文昭仁憲孝皇帝，諱構，字德基，徽宗第九子，母曰顯仁皇后韋氏。

translations.literal: Gaozong, the emperor who received the mandate, restored the dynasty, accomplished full merit, utmost virtue, sage, divine, martial, literary, illustrious, benevolent, constitutional, and filial—taboo name Gou, courtesy name Deji—was Huizong’s ninth son; his mother was Empress Xianren of the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong—Received-the-Mandate, Restored-the-Dynasty, Full-Merit, Utmost-Virtue, Sage, Divine, Martial, Literary, Illustrious, Benevolent, Constitutional, Filial—taboo Gou, style Deji, Huizong’s ninth son, born of Empress Xianren Wei.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年五月乙巳生東京之大內，赤光照室。

translations.literal: Daguan year 1, fifth month, day yisi: he was born in the great inner palace at Dongjing; red light filled the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Daguan 1, fifth month, yisi: born in Dongjing’s inner palace; red light washed the room.

sentences.zh: 八月丁丑，賜名，授定武軍節度使、檢校太尉，封蜀國公。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day dingchou: a name was granted; he was made military commissioner of Dingwu army, checked Grand General, and enfeoffed Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, dingchou: named and made Dingwu commissioner, Grand General, Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 二年正月庚申，封廣平郡王。

translations.literal: Year 2, first month, day gengshen: he was advanced to Prince of Guangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2, first month, gengshen: Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年十二月壬子，進封康王。

translations.literal: Xuanhe year 3, twelfth month, day renzi: he was advanced to Prince of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhe 3, twelfth month, renzi: Prince of Kang.

sentences.zh: 資性朗悟，博學強記，讀書日誦千餘言，挽弓至一石五鬥。

translations.literal: By nature bright and quick, he studied widely and remembered strongly, reciting more than a thousand characters a day in reading, and drawing the bow to one stone five pecks.
translations.idiomatic: Bright of wit, deep in learning and memory, he recited a thousand characters a day and drew the bow to one stone five pecks.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，始冠，出就外第。

translations.literal: Xuanhe year 4: he received the capping rite and went out to an outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhe 4: capped, he moved to an outer mansion.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年春正月，金人犯京師，軍於城西北，遣使入城，邀親王、宰臣議和軍中。

translations.literal: Jingkang year 1, spring, first month: Jin men attacked the capital; their army camped northwest of the city and sent envoys in, inviting imperial princes and chief ministers to discuss peace in the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkang 1, spring: Jin struck the capital, camped northwest, and called princes and chief ministers into camp to treat for peace.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方遣同知樞密院事李棁等使金，議割太原、中山、河間三鎮，遣宰臣授地，親王送大軍過河。

translations.literal: The court was then sending Associate Director of Military Affairs Li Zhan and others to Jin to discuss ceding Taiyuan, Zhongshan, and Hejian—the three circuits—and dispatching chief ministers to hand over territory and an imperial prince to escort the great army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The court had sent Li Zhan and others to Jin to offer Taiyuan, Zhongshan, and Hejian and to send ministers to surrender land and a prince to escort the army across the river.

sentences.zh: 欽宗召帝諭指，帝慷慨請行。

translations.literal: Qinzong summoned the prince and instructed him; the prince volunteered boldly to go.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzong briefed Prince Kang; the prince asked to go himself.

sentences.zh: 遂命少宰張邦昌為計議使，與帝俱。

translations.literal: Junior Chancellor Zhang Bangchang was then made planning commissioner and went with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang was made planning commissioner and accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 金帥斡離不留之軍中旬日，帝意氣閒暇。

translations.literal: Jin commander Wolibu kept him in camp half a month; the prince’s bearing remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu held him in camp a fortnight; Prince Kang’s manner never frayed.

sentences.zh: 二月，會京畿宣撫司都統制姚平仲夜襲金人砦不克，金人見責，邦昌恐懼涕泣，帝不為動，斡離不異之，更請肅王。

translations.literal: Second month: Capital-District Pacification commander Yao Pingzhong raided the Jin camp by night and failed; the Jin rebuked them; Bangchang wept in fear, but the prince was unmoved—Wolibu marveled and asked instead for Prince Su.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: Yao Pingzhong’s night raid on the Jin camp failed; the Jin upbraided them; Bangchang wept, but the prince did not stir—Wolibu, wondering, demanded Prince Su instead.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，肅王至軍中，許割三鎮地。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Prince Su reached the camp and the three circuits’ lands were promised.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Prince Su came to camp and the three circuits were granted.

sentences.zh: 進邦昌為太宰，留質軍中，帝始得還。

translations.literal: Bangchang was advanced to Grand Chancellor and left as hostage in camp; the prince was at last allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang became grand chancellor and stayed as hostage; Prince Kang was released.

sentences.zh: 金兵退，復遣給事中王雲使金，以租賦贖三鎮地。

translations.literal: When the Jin withdrew, Supervising Secretariat Attendant Wang Yun was again sent to Jin to ransom the three circuits with rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin withdrew, Wang Yun went again to Jin to buy back the three circuits with tribute.

sentences.zh: 又以蠟書結遼降將耶律餘睹，為金人所得。

translations.literal: A wax-sealed letter was also used to win over the surrendered Liao general Yelü Yudu; the Jin seized it.
translations.idiomatic: A secret letter to win Yelü Yudu, a Liao turncoat, fell into Jin hands.

sentences.zh: 八月，金帥粘罕復引兵深入，陷太原。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Jin commander Nianhan again led troops deep in; Taiyuan fell.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Nianhan drove deep again and took Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 斡離不破真定。

translations.literal: Wolibu broke Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu overran Zhending.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，王雲從吏自金先還，言金人須帝再至乃議和。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Wang Yun’s clerks returned from Jin ahead of him, saying the Jin required the prince to come again before they would discuss peace.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month: Yun’s clerks came back from Jin first, reporting peace would wait until the prince returned.

sentences.zh: 雲歸，言金人堅欲得地，不然，進兵取汴都。

translations.literal: When Yun returned, he said the Jin insisted on having the land; otherwise they would advance on Bian, the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yun returned saying the Jin would have the land or march on Bian.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔帝使河北，奉袞冕、玉輅，尊金主為伯，上尊號十八字。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: an edict ordered the prince to Hebei, bearing imperial robes, the jade chariot, and an eighteen-character honorific title making the Jin ruler “elder uncle.”
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: the prince was sent to Hebei with imperial robes, the jade chariot, and an eighteen-character style naming the Jin ruler elder uncle.

sentences.zh: 被命，即發京師。

translations.literal: On receiving the order he set out from the capital at once.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital the moment the order came.

sentences.zh: 以門下侍郎耿南仲主和議，請與俱，乃以其子中書舍人延禧為參議官偕行。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery Geng Nanzhong favored peace and asked to go along; his son, Secretariat Drafter Yanxi, was made planning commissioner to travel with them.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong, who sought peace, went along; his son Yanxi served as planning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝由滑、浚至磁州，守臣宗澤請曰：「肅王去不返，金兵已迫，復去何益？

translations.literal: The prince went by Hua, Jun, and to Cizhou; defender Zong Ze pleaded: “Prince Su went and did not return; the Jin are already pressing—what good is going again?
translations.idiomatic: By Hua and Jun to Cizhou, Zong Ze pleaded: Prince Su never came back, and the Jin are at our heels—what use is going again?

sentences.zh: 請留磁。

translations.literal: Please remain at Ci.”
translations.idiomatic: Stay at Ci.

sentences.zh: 」磁人以雲將挾帝入金，遂殺雲。

translations.literal: The people of Ci, believing Yun would drag the prince into Jin, killed Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Ci’s people, fearing Yun would deliver the prince to the Jin, killed Yun.

sentences.zh: 時粘罕、斡離不已率兵渡河，相繼圍京師。

translations.literal: By then Nianhan and Wolibu had already crossed the river and were besieging the capital in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan and Wolibu had crossed the river and were tightening siege on the capital.

sentences.zh: 從者以磁不可留，知相州汪伯彥亦以蠟書請帝還相州。

translations.literal: His followers said Ci could not be held; Xiang prefecture defender Wang Boyan also sent a secret letter asking the prince to return to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His train said Ci was unsafe; Wang Boyan of Xiang urged him back by secret letter.

sentences.zh: 閏月，耿南仲馳至相，見帝致辭，以面受欽宗之旨，盡起河北兵入衛，帝乃同南仲募兵勤王。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Geng Nanzhong galloped to Xiang, saw the prince, and excused himself, saying he had received Qinzong’s command in person to raise all Hebei troops for the capital’s defense; the prince then joined Nanzhong in recruiting troops to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Nanzhong raced to Xiang, excused himself, and said Qinzong had ordered every Hebei soldier to the capital; the prince joined him in raising rescue armies.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷聞金兵渡河，欲拜帝為元帥。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court heard the Jin had crossed the river, it wished to appoint the prince commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the Jin had crossed, the court had meant to make him commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至是，殿中侍御史胡唐老復申元帥之議，尚書右僕射何㮚拟詔書以進，欽宗遣閣門祗候秦仔持蠟詔至相，拜帝為河北兵馬大元帥，知中山府陳亨伯為元帥，汪伯彥、宗澤為副元帥。

translations.literal: Now Palace Attendant Hu Tanglao renewed the commander proposal; Right Vice Director He 㮚 drafted the edict for presentation; Qinzong sent Palace Door Attendant Qin Zai with a wax edict to Xiang, appointing the prince Great Commander of Hebei military forces, Chen Hengbo of Zhongshan as commander, and Wang Boyan and Zong Ze as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tanglao pressed the commander plan again; He 㮚 drafted the edict; Qin Zai brought a wax seal to Xiang making Prince Kang Great Commander of Hebei, Chen Hengbo commander, Wang Boyan and Zong Ze deputies.

sentences.zh: 仔於頂發中出詔，帝讀之嗚咽，兵民感動。

translations.literal: Zai drew the edict from his topknot; the prince read it with sobs; soldiers and people were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zai pulled the edict from his hair; the prince read it weeping; army and people wept with him.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬戌朔，帝開大元帥府，有兵萬人，分為五軍，命武顯大夫陳淬都統制軍馬。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day renxu new moon: the prince opened the Great Commander headquarters with ten thousand men, divided into five armies, and ordered Military Display Grand Master Chen Cui to command all forces.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, renxu new moon: he opened headquarters with ten thousand men in five armies and put Chen Cui over the host.

sentences.zh: 閣門祗候侯章齎蠟書至自京師，詔帝盡發河北兵，命守臣自將。

translations.literal: Palace Door Attendant Hou Zhang brought a wax letter from the capital ordering the prince to send out every Hebei soldier and command local defenders to lead in person.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhang came from the capital with wax orders to empty Hebei of troops and make every prefect lead his own men.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下令諸郡守與諸將，議引兵渡河。

translations.literal: The prince then ordered prefects and generals to discuss crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered prefects and generals to plan a crossing.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝率兵離相州。

translations.literal: Day yihai: the prince led the army away from Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, he marched out of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 丙子，履冰渡河。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: he crossed the ice on the river.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, he crossed the river on the ice.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，次大名府。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: he halted at Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, he made Daming.

sentences.zh: 宗澤以二千人先諸軍至，知信德府梁揚祖以三千人繼至，張俊、苗傅、楊沂中、田師中皆在麾下，兵威稍振。

translations.literal: Zong Ze came first with two thousand men; Xinde prefect Liang Yangzu followed with three thousand; Zhang Jun, Miao Fu, Yang Yizhong, and Tian Shizhong were all in his train—the army’s spirit lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze led two thousand ahead; Liang Yangzu of Xinde brought three thousand after; Zhang Jun, Miao Fu, Yang Yizhong, and Tian Shizhong rode with him, and the host found its spine.

sentences.zh: 會簽書樞密院事曹輔齎蠟詔至，云金人登城不下，方議和好，可屯兵近甸，毋輕動。

translations.literal: Signatory of Military Affairs Cao Fu arrived with a wax edict saying the Jin had mounted the walls but not descended and were discussing peace; he might camp the army in the near suburbs and not stir lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fu came with wax word that the Jin sat on the walls yet talked peace—camp near the capital, do not stir rashly.

sentences.zh: 汪伯彥等皆信和議，惟宗澤請直趨澶淵為壁，次第解京城之圍。

translations.literal: Wang Boyan and the rest trusted the peace talks; only Zong Ze asked to strike straight for Chanyuan as a bastion and lift the siege step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan and the peace party prevailed in counsel; only Zong Ze urged a dash to Chanyuan to break the siege ring by ring.

sentences.zh: 伯彥、南仲請移軍東平。

translations.literal: Boyan and Nanzhong asked to shift the army to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan and Nanzhong wanted Dongping.

sentences.zh: 帝遂遣澤以萬人進屯澶淵，揚言帝在軍中。

translations.literal: The prince then sent Zong Ze forward with ten thousand men to camp at Chanyuan, proclaiming that the prince was with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zong Ze with ten thousand to Chanyuan, crying that the prince himself was in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 自是澤不復預府中謀議。

translations.literal: From then on Zong Ze no longer joined headquarters counsel.
translations.idiomatic: After that Zong Ze sat outside headquarters debate.

sentences.zh: 帝決意趨東平。

translations.literal: The prince resolved to hurry to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang set his face for Dongping.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝發大名。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: the prince left Daming.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, he left Daming.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年春正月癸巳，帝至東平。

translations.literal: Jianyan year 1, spring, first month, day guisi: the prince reached Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan 1, spring, guisi: he reached Dongping.

sentences.zh: 初，帝軍在相州，京城圍久，中外莫知帝處。

translations.literal: Earlier, while the prince’s army was at Xiang, the capital had been besieged long; inside and outside none knew where he was.
translations.idiomatic: While he was at Xiang the capital had languished under siege and none knew where the prince lay.

sentences.zh: 及是，陳請四集，取決帥府。

translations.literal: Now petitions poured in from every quarter, seeking decision from the commander’s headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Now memorials flooded headquarters, begging a commander’s word.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，高陽關路安撫使黃潛善、總管楊惟忠亦部兵數千至東平。

translations.literal: Day renyin: Gaoyang Pass pacification commissioner Huang Qianshan and commander Yang Weizhong also brought several thousand men to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Huang Qianshan and Yang Weizhong brought several thousand more to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 命潛善進屯興仁，留惟忠為元帥都統制。

translations.literal: Qianshan was ordered to advance and camp at Xingren; Weizhong was kept as commander headquarters commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan camped at Xingren; Weizhong stayed as headquarters commander.

sentences.zh: 金人聞帝在澶淵，遣甲士及中書舍人張澂來召。

translations.literal: Hearing the prince was at Chanyuan, the Jin sent armored men and Secretariat Drafter Zhang Cheng to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning he was at Chanyuan, the Jin sent armor and Zhang Cheng to call him in.

sentences.zh: 宗澤命壯士射之，澂乃遁。

translations.literal: Zong Ze ordered stalwarts to shoot at them; Cheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze had bowmen pepper them; Cheng ran.

sentences.zh: 伯彥等請帝如濟州。

translations.literal: Boyan and the rest asked the prince to go to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan urged Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 二月庚辰，發東平。

translations.literal: Second month, day gengchen: he set out from Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, gengchen: he marched from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 癸未，次濟州。

translations.literal: Day guimao: he halted at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, he reached Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 時帥府官軍及群盜來歸者號百萬人，分屯濟、濮諸州府，而諸路勤王兵不得進。

translations.literal: By then headquarters regulars and bandits who had come over were said to number a million, camped across Ji and Pu prefectures and circuits, while relief armies from the routes could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters and turncoat bands were called a million, scattered through Ji and Pu, while route relief armies stalled on the roads.

sentences.zh: 二帝已在金人軍中。

translations.literal: Both emperors were already in the Jin camp.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong and Qinzong were already Jin prisoners.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，金人立張邦昌為帝，稱大楚。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingyou: the Jin set up Zhang Bangchang as emperor, styling the state Great Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, dingyou: the Jin made Zhang Bangchang emperor of Great Chu.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善以告，帝慟哭，僚屬欲奉帝駐軍宿州，謀渡江左，帝聞三軍籍籍，遂輒。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan reported it; the prince wept; his staff wished to hold the army at Suzhou and cross to the lands south of the Yangtze, but hearing the three armies murmuring, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan brought word; the prince wept; his staff urged Suzhou and a crossing south of the river, but the armies’ murmur checked him.

sentences.zh: 承制以宗澤為徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: By provisional order Zong Ze was made Huaiyou Pavilion awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zong Ze Huaiyou Pavilion attendant by provisional order.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，斡離不退師，徽宗北遷。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: Wolibu withdrew; Huizong was moved north.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Wolibu drew off and Huizong was marched north.

sentences.zh: 戊午，承制以汪伯彥為顯謨閣待制，充元帥；

translations.literal: Day wuwu: by provisional order Wang Boyan was made Xianmo Pavilion attendant and served as commander;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Boyan was made Xianmo attendant and commander by provisional order;

sentences.zh: 潛善為徽猷閣待制，充副元帥。

translations.literal: Qianshan was made Huaiyou Pavilion attendant and served as deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan was Huaiyou attendant and deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，粘罕退師，欽宗北遷。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Nianhan withdrew; Qinzong was moved north.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: Nianhan withdrew; Qinzong followed north.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，邦昌尊元祐皇后為宋太后，遣人至濟州訪帝，又遣吏部尚書謝克家來迎。

translations.literal: Day guihai: Bangchang honored the Yuanyou empress as Song dowager, sent men to Jizhou to seek the prince, and dispatched Minister of Personnel Xie Kejia to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Bangchang styled the Yuanyou empress Song dowager, sought the prince at Jizhou, and sent Xie Kejia to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 耿南仲率幕僚勸進，帝避席流涕，遜辭不受。

translations.literal: Geng Nanzhong and the staff urged accession; the prince left his seat weeping and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong and the staff pressed the throne; the prince wept and refused.

sentences.zh: 伯彥等引天命人心為請，且謂靖康紀元，為十二月立康之兆。

translations.literal: Boyan and the rest cited heaven’s will and the people’s hearts, saying the Jingkang reign title was an omen set in the twelfth month to raise the Prince of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan pleaded mandate and folk, saying Jingkang’s name and the twelfth month foretold the Prince of Kang.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「當更思之。

translations.literal: The prince said: “I must think again.”
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: I must think again.

sentences.zh: 」以知淮甯府趙子崧為寶文閣學士、元帥府參議官、東南道總管，統東南勤王兵。

translations.literal: Huaining prefect Zhao Zisong was made Baowen Hall academician, headquarters planning commissioner, and Southeast Route commander to gather southeast relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zisong of Huaining became Baowen academician, planning commissioner, and Southeast Route commander to gather southern relief.

sentences.zh: 邦昌遣閣門宣贊舍人蔣師愈等持書詣帝，自言從權濟事，及將歸寶避位之意。

translations.literal: Bangchang sent Palace Gate Proclamation Attendant Jiang Shiyu and others with a letter to the prince, saying he had followed expedience and meant to return the jewel and yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang’s letter through Jiang Shiyu said he had ruled from necessity and would yield the jewel and step down.

sentences.zh: 帝亦貽諸帥書，以未得至京，已至者毋輒入。

translations.literal: The prince also sent letters to the commanders, saying that since he had not reached the capital, those already there must not enter rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the commanders: until he reached the capital, none already there should march in.

sentences.zh: 聞資政殿大學士、領開封府事李綱在湖北，遣劉默持書訪之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Grand Academician and Kaifeng metropolitan governor Li Gang was in Hubei, he sent Liu Mo with a letter to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Li Gang was in Hubei, he sent Liu Mo to seek him.

sentences.zh: 又諭宗澤等，以受偽命之人義當誅討，然慮事出權宜，未可輕動。

translations.literal: He also instructed Zong Ze and the rest that men who had accepted the false mandate deserved execution, yet he feared the matter was expedient and they should not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zong Ze that collaborators deserved death, yet the throne feared rash strokes against men acting under duress.

sentences.zh: 澤復書謂邦昌篡亂蹤跡已無可疑，宜早正天位，興復社稷，不可不斷。

translations.literal: Zong Ze replied that Bangchang’s usurpation left no doubt; the heavenly throne should be set right early and the altars restored—the matter could not wait.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze answered that Bangchang’s treason was plain; the throne must be taken and the altars raised without delay.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎呂好問亦以蠟書來，言帝不自立，恐有不當立而立者。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery Lü Haowen also sent a secret letter, saying if the prince did not rise, someone unfit might.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Haowen wrote in secret: if the prince would not reign, another might.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，謝克家以「大宋受命之寶」至濟州，帝慟哭跪受，命克家還京師，趣辦儀物。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: Xie Kejia brought the “Great Song Mandate Jewel” to Jizhou; the prince wept, knelt to receive it, and ordered Kejia back to the capital to prepare regalia.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Kejia brought the Great Song Mandate Jewel; the prince knelt weeping, received it, and sent Kejia to ready the rites.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，濟州父老詣軍門，言州四旁望見城中火光屬天，請帝即位於濟。

translations.literal: Day wuchen: Jizhou elders came to headquarters, saying fires ringed the city on every side and asked that he ascend at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Jizhou elders saw firelight on every horizon and begged him to reign at Ji.

sentences.zh: 會宗澤來言，南京乃藝祖興王之地，取四方中，漕運尤易。

translations.literal: Zong Ze came and said Nanjing was where the founding ancestor had risen, central to the four quarters and easiest for grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze argued Nanjing, Taizu’s founding ground, sat at the realm’s center and drew grain easiest.

sentences.zh: 遂決意趨應天。

translations.literal: He then resolved to go to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He set his face for Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 是夕，邦昌手書上延福宮太后尊號曰元祐皇后，入居禁中，以尚書左丞馮澥為奉迎使。

translations.literal: That night Bangchang wrote by hand to the empress at Yanfu Palace with the Yuanyou title; she entered the inner palace; Left Vice Director Feng Yi was made welcome commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bangchang wrote the Yuanyou title for the empress at Yanfu; she entered the palace; Feng Yi welcomed her.

sentences.zh: 皇后又遣兄子衛尉少卿孟忠厚持手書遺帝。

translations.literal: The empress also sent her elder brother’s son, Vice Minister of the Guard Meng Zhonghou, with a hand letter to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The empress sent her nephew Meng Zhonghou with a letter in her own hand.

sentences.zh: 皇后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: The empress held court behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ruled from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 邦昌權尚書左僕射，率在京百官上表勸進，不許。

translations.literal: Bangchang, acting Left Vice Director, led the capital officials in memorials urging accession; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang, acting left vice director, led the capital in urging the throne; again refused.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，皇后手書告中外，俾帝嗣統。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: the empress wrote by hand to announce within and without, bidding the prince succeed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the empress wrote to all under heaven bidding him succeed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，百官再上表，又不許。

translations.literal: Day yihai: the officials memorialized again; again it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the officials memorialized again; again refused.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，馮澥等至濟州，百官三上表，許以權聽國事。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: Feng Yi and the rest reached Jizhou; on the officials’ third memorial he permitted provisional rule.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Feng Yi reached Jizhou; on the third memorial he allowed provisional rule.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，命宗澤先勒兵分駐長垣、韋城等縣，以備非常。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: he ordered Zong Ze first to press troops to Changyuan, Weicheng, and other counties against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, he sent Zong Ze to plant garrisons at Changyuan and Weicheng against surprise.

sentences.zh: 東道副總管朱勝非至濟州，宣撫司統制官韓世忠以兵來會。

translations.literal: Eastern Route deputy commander Zhu Shengfei reached Jizhou; Pacification headquarters commander Han Shizhong brought troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei came to Jizhou; Han Shizhong joined with his command.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝發濟州，鄜延副總管劉光世自陝州來會，以光世為五軍都提舉。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: the prince left Jizhou; Yan’an deputy commander Liu Guangshi came from Shaan to join and was made commander over the five armies.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, he left Jizhou; Liu Guangshi came from Shaan and took the five armies.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，次單州。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: he halted at Shan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Shan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，次虞城縣。

translations.literal: Day renwu: he halted at Yucheng county.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 西道都總管王襄自襄陽來會。

translations.literal: Western Route commander Wang Xiang came from Xiangyang to join.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang came from Xiangyang to join.

sentences.zh: 癸未，至應天府。

translations.literal: Day guimao: he reached Yingtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 皇后詔有司備法駕儀仗。

translations.literal: The empress ordered the offices to prepare imperial regalia and guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ordered regalia and guard of honor made ready.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，張邦昌至，伏地慟 哭請死，帝慰撫之。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Zhang Bangchang arrived, prostrated himself weeping and begging death; the prince comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Bangchang came, lay weeping and begged death; the prince raised him up.

sentences.zh: 承制以汪伯彥為顯謨閣直學士，黃潛善為徽猷閣直學士。

translations.literal: By provisional order Wang Boyan was made Xianmo Pavilion academician and Huang Qianshan Huaiyou Pavilion academician.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan became Xianmo academician; Qianshan, Huaiyou academician, by provisional order.

sentences.zh: 權吏部尚書王時雍等奉乘輿服禦至，群臣勸進者益眾，命有司築壇府門之左。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Personnel Wang Shiyong and others brought the imperial carriage robes; those urging accession grew more numerous; the offices were ordered to build an altar left of the prefectural gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong brought the imperial robes; the urging crowd swelled; an altar was raised left of the gate.

sentences.zh: 五月庚寅朔，帝登壇受命，禮畢慟哭，遙謝二帝，即位於府治。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day gengyin new moon: the prince ascended the altar, received the mandate, finished the rites weeping, bowed from afar to the two emperors, and took the throne in the prefectural hall.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, gengyin new moon: he mounted the altar, took the mandate, wept through the rite, bowed to the captive emperors afar, and reigned from the prefectural hall.

sentences.zh: 改元建炎。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Jianyan.
translations.idiomatic: The reign was styled Jianyan.

sentences.zh: 大赦，常赦所不原者咸赦除之。

translations.literal: A great amnesty; even those regular amnesties did not pardon were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Great amnesty—even crimes ordinary pardons spared were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌及應于供奉金國之人，一切不問。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang and all who had attended on the Jin were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang and every man who had served the Jin went untouched.

sentences.zh: 命西京留守司修奉祖宗陵寢。

translations.literal: The Western Capital garrison was ordered to repair the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Capital garrison was told to tend the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 罷天下神霄宮。

translations.literal: Spirit Marvel palaces throughout the realm were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Marvel palaces empire-wide were shut.

sentences.zh: 住散青苗錢。

translations.literal: Green Sprout loans were halted and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprout loans were stopped and written off.

sentences.zh: 應死節及歿于王事者並推恩。

translations.literal: Those who died loyal and those who died in the state’s service were all granted favor.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal dead and dead in the state’s service were honored.

sentences.zh: 奉使未還者，祿其家一年。

translations.literal: Envoys not yet returned had their households paid one year’s salary.
translations.idiomatic: Families of envoys still abroad were paid a year’s stipend.

sentences.zh: 應選人並循資，已系承直郎者，改次等京官。

translations.literal: All examination candidates advanced in grade; those already at Assistant Director rank were promoted one grade in capital office.
translations.idiomatic: Examination candidates advanced a grade; men at Assistant Director rose one capital rank.

sentences.zh: 臣僚因亂去官者，限一月還任。

translations.literal: Officials who had fled office in the turmoil were given one month to return.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who had fled the chaos had one month to return to post.

sentences.zh: 潰兵、群資咸許自新。

translations.literal: Routed soldiers and scattered assets were all permitted to make a new start.
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops and scattered goods could start clean.

sentences.zh: 免系官欠負，蠲南京及元帥府常駐軍一月以上州縣夏稅。

translations.literal: State debts were forgiven; summer tax for Nanjing and prefectures where headquarters troops had stayed a month or more was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: State debts were cancelled; summer tax was remitted for Nanjing and any prefecture that had fed headquarters a month.

sentences.zh: 應天府特奏名舉人並與同進士出身，免解人與免省試。

translations.literal: Special-entry candidates of Yingtian were given jinshi standing; those exempt from the qualifying exam were exempt from the provincial exam.
translations.idiomatic: Yingtian special-entry men were made jinshi; exam exemptions carried to the provincial test.

sentences.zh: 諸路特奏名三舉以上及宗室嘗預貢者，並推恩。

translations.literal: On every route, special-entry men with three attempts or more and clansmen who had once presented tribute were all granted favor.
translations.idiomatic: Route men with three special entries and clansmen who had once presented tribute received favor.

sentences.zh: 應募兵勤王人以兵付州縣主兵官，聽赴行在。

translations.literal: Men who had raised troops to rescue the throne were to hand their soldiers to prefectural commanders and were permitted to come to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue levies were to be handed to prefectural commanders; the men might follow the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 中外臣庶許言民間疾苦，雖詆訐亦不加罪。

translations.literal: Within and without, commoners and officials might speak the people’s hardships; even slander went unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country might speak folk hardship; even slander went free.

sentences.zh: 命官犯罪，更不取特旨裁斷。

translations.literal: Crimes by appointed officials were no longer to be judged by special imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Official crimes would no longer be settled by special edict.

sentences.zh: 蔡京、童貫、朱勔、李彥、孟昌齡、梁師成、譚稹及其子孫，更不收敘。

translations.literal: Cai Jing, Tong Guan, Zhu Mian, Li Yan, Meng Changling, Liang Shicheng, Tan Zhen, and their descendants were never again to be reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, Tong Guan, Zhu Mian, Li Yan, Meng Changling, Liang Shicheng, Tan Zhen, and their lines were barred forever.

sentences.zh: 內外大臣，限十日各舉布衣有材略者一人。

translations.literal: Inner and outer great ministers were given ten days each to recommend one commoner of talent and plan.
translations.idiomatic: Every great minister had ten days to name one able commoner.

sentences.zh: 餘如故事。

translations.literal: The rest followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed old law.

sentences.zh: 以黃潛善為中書侍郎，汪伯彥同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wang Boyan Associate Director of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan took the secretariat; Boyan, associate director of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元祐皇后在東京，是日徹簾。

translations.literal: The Yuanyou empress was at Dongjing; that day the curtain was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongjing the Yuanyou empress withdrew from the curtain that day.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，遙尊乾龍皇帝為孝慈淵聖皇帝，元祐皇后為元祐太后。

translations.literal: Day xinmao: from afar Huizong was honored Sagely, Filial, and Profound Emperor; the Yuanyou empress was honored Yuanyou Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Huizong was hailed from afar Sagely Filial Profound Emperor; the empress, Yuanyou Dowager.

sentences.zh: 詔史官辨宣仁聖烈皇后誣謗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the historians to clear the slander against Empress Xuanren the Sagely and Liege.
translations.idiomatic: Historians were ordered to clear the slander on Empress Xuanren the Sagely and Liege.

sentences.zh: 築景靈宮于江寧府。

translations.literal: The Spirit Scene Palace was built at Jiangning prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Scene Palace rose at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以張邦昌為太保、奉國軍節度使、同安郡王，五日一赴都堂參決大事。

translations.literal: Day renchen: Zhang Bangchang was made Grand Guardian, military commissioner of Fengguo army, and Prince of Tong’an commandery, attending the chief council five days of ten to decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Bangchang became grand guardian, Fengguo commissioner, Prince of Tong’an, attending council five days in ten.

sentences.zh: 以河東、北宣撫使范訥為京城留守。

translations.literal: Hebei-east pacification commissioner Fan Nuo was made capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Nuo of Hebei-east pacification held the capital.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，遙尊帝母韋賢妃為宣和皇后，遙立嘉國夫人邢氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Day guisi: from afar the emperor’s mother, Worthy Consort Wei, was honored Xuanhe Empress; Lady Xing of Jia state was established empress from afar.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Consort Wei was hailed Xuanhe Empress; Lady Xing of Jia was named empress from afar.

sentences.zh: 耿南仲罷。

translations.literal: Geng Nanzhong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong left office.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以李綱為尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎，趣赴行在，楊惟忠為建武軍節度使，主管殿前司公事。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: Li Gang was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, urged to the mobile court; Yang Weizhong was made military commissioner of Jianwu army and overseer of Palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Li Gang took right secretariat and chancellery and was summoned to court; Weizhong took Jianwu and the Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷諸盜及民兵之為統制者，簡其士馬隸五軍。

translations.literal: Command over bandits and militia was abolished; their men and horses were sifted into the five armies.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit and militia commands were struck; their horses and men were sifted into the five armies.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以生辰為天申節。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: his birthday was made the Tian Shen festival.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, his birthday became the Tian Shen festival.

sentences.zh: 馮澥罷，以兵部尚書呂好問為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Feng Yi was dismissed; Minister of War Lü Haowen was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi left; Lü Haowen of War became right vice director.

sentences.zh: 命中軍統制馬忠、後軍統制張昪率兵萬人，趣河間府追襲金人。

translations.literal: Center Army commander Ma Zhong and Rear Army commander Zhang Bian were ordered to lead ten thousand men to Hejian to pursue the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhong of the Center and Zhang Bian of the Rear took ten thousand to chase the Jin toward Hejian.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以呂好問兼門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: Lü Haowen was made concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Lü Haowen also took the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以黃潛善兼禦營使，汪伯彥副之，真定府路副總管王淵為都統制，鄜延路副總管劉光世提舉一行事務。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: Huang Qianshan was made concurrent Imperial Camp commissioner and Wang Boyan his deputy; Zhending Route deputy commander Wang Yuan was made overall commander; Yan’an deputy Liu Guangshi was made overseer of the traveling court’s affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Qianshan took the Imperial Camp with Boyan as deputy; Wang Yuan commanded; Liu Guangshi ran the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 王時雍黃州安置。

translations.literal: Wang Shiyong was settled at Huang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong was sent to Huang.

sentences.zh: 命統制官薛廣、張瓊率兵六千人會河北山水砦義兵，共復磁、相。

translations.literal: Commanders Xue Guang and Zhang Qiong were ordered to lead six thousand men to join Hebei mountain-fort militia and together recover Ci and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guang and Zhang Qiong took six thousand to join Hebei mountain militia and retake Ci and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以資政殿學士路允迪為京城撫諭使，龍圖閣學士耿延禧副之。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance Lu Yundi was made capital pacification commissioner; Dragon Hall academician Geng Yanxi was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Lu Yundi pacified the capital with Geng Yanxi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部侍郎李若水觀文殿學士，諡忠湣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Li Ruoshui was posthumously made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruoshui was posthumously grand academician Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 己亥，召太學生陳東赴行在。

translations.literal: Day jihai: Imperial University student Chen Dong was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Chen Dong of the university was called to court.

sentences.zh: 李綱至江寧，誅叛卒周德等。

translations.literal: When Li Gang reached Jiangning he executed the mutineer Zhou De and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangning Li Gang executed the mutineer Zhou De and his men.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔：以靖康大臣主和誤國，責李邦彥為建寧軍節度副使、潯州安置，徙吳敏柳州，蔡懋英州。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: an edict—Jingkang ministers who had favored peace and ruined the state: Li Bangyan was made military vice commissioner of Jianning army and settled at Xun; Wu Min was moved to Liuzhou; Cai Mao to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, peace ministers of Jingkang were punished: Li Bangyan to Xun, Wu Min to Liuzhou, Cai Mao to Ying.

sentences.zh: 李棁、宇文虛中、鄭望之、李鄴皆以使金請割地，責廣南諸州並安置。

translations.literal: Li Zhan, Yuwen Xuzhong, Zheng Wangzhi, and Li Ye had all asked to cede land on embassy to Jin and were settled across the southern circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan, Yuwen Xuzhong, Zheng Wangzhi, and Li Ye, who had sued for cession in Jin, were scattered through the south.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，詔張邦昌知幾達變，勳在社稷，如文彥博例，月兩赴都堂。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: an edict—Zhang Bangchang knew the moment and turned with the times; his merit to the altars matched Wen Yanbo’s precedent; twice a month he was to attend the chief council.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Bangchang was praised for reading the hour; like Wen Yanbo he would attend council twice a month.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，封後宮潘氏為賢妃。

translations.literal: Day renyin: Lady Pan of the inner quarters was made Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Lady Pan became Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 以江、淮發運使梁揚祖提領東南茶鹽事。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai transport commissioner Liang Yangzu was put in charge of southeast tea and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yangzu took southeast tea and salt.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，天申節，罷百官上壽。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Tian Shen festival; officials’ birthday congratulations were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Tian Shen day—court birthday rites were cancelled.

sentences.zh: 乙己，賜諸路勤王兵還營者錢，人三千。

translations.literal: Day yiji: relief troops returning to camp on every route were given three thousand cash each man.
translations.idiomatic: On yiji, every relief soldier going home was paid three thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以誣謗宣仁聖烈皇后，追貶蔡確、蔡卞、邢怒、蔡懋官。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: for slandering Empress Xuanren the Sagely and Liege, Cai Que, Cai Bian, Xing Nu, and Cai Mao were further demoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Cai Que, Cai Bian, Xing Nu, and Cai Mao were demoted again for slandering Empress Xuanren.

sentences.zh: 以保靜軍節度使姚古知河 南府。

translations.literal: Baojing army military commissioner Yao Gu was made prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gu of Baojing took Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金人陷河中府，權府事郝仲連死之。

translations.literal: The Jin took Hezhong prefecture; acting prefect Hao Zhonglian died.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Hezhong; Hao Zhonglian died holding it.

sentences.zh: 丁未，徽宗至燕山府。

translations.literal: Day dingwei: Huizong reached Yanshan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Huizong reached Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以宗澤為龍圖閣學士、知襄陽府。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: Zong Ze was made Dragon Hall academician and prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Zong Ze became dragon academician and Xiangyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 壬子，進張邦昌太傅。

translations.literal: Day renzi: Zhang Bangchang was advanced to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Bangchang rose to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，罷監察御史張所，尋責江州安置。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: Supervising Censor Zhang Suo was dismissed and soon settled at Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Zhang Suo left the censorate and was sent to Jiang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔成都、京兆、襄陽、荊南、江甯府、鄧、揚二州儲資糧，修城壘，以備巡幸。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: an edict—Chengdu, Jingzhao, Xiangyang, Jingnan, Jiangning, Deng and Yang prefectures were to store grain and funds and repair walls against an imperial tour.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Chengdu, Jingzhao, Xiangyang, Jingnan, Jiangning, Deng, and Yang were told to hoard grain, money, and walls for a possible tour.

sentences.zh: 以簽書樞密院事張叔夜嘗援京城力戰，從徽宗北行，遙命為觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Signatory of Military Affairs Zhang Shuye, who had fought hard to aid the capital and followed Huizong north, was from afar made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and commissioner of Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuye, who had bled for the capital and marched north with Huizong, was hailed from afar grand academician and Liquan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戊午，右諫議大夫范宗尹罷。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: Right Remonstrance Commissioner Fan Zongyin was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Fan Zongyin left the remonstrance bureau.

sentences.zh: 遣太常少卿周望使河北軍前通問二帝。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Rites Zhou Wang was sent to the Hebei front to inquire after the two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wang of Rites was sent to Hebei to ask after the captive emperors.

sentences.zh: 西道總管王襄、北道總管趙野坐勤王稽緩，並分司，襄陽府、青州居住。

translations.literal: Western Route commander Wang Xiang and Northern Route commander Zhao Ye were punished for slow relief—both made branch officials, Xiang at Xiangyang and Ye at Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang and Zhao Ye, slow to rescue, were made branch officials at Xiangyang and Qing.

sentences.zh: 尋責襄永州、野邵州，並安置。

translations.literal: Soon Xiang was sent to Yong and Ye to Shao, both settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xiang was moved to Yong and Ye to Shao.

sentences.zh: 六月己未朔，李綱入見，上十議，曰國是、巡幸、赦令、僭逆、偽命、戰、守、本政、責成、修德。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiwei new moon: Li Gang had audience and presented ten proposals—National Policy, Imperial Tour, Amnesty, Usurpation, False Mandate, War, Defense, Root Government, Fix Responsibility, Cultivate Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, jiwei new moon: Li Gang presented ten policies—national aim, tour, amnesty, usurpation, false mandate, war, defense, root government, accountability, and virtue.

sentences.zh: 以前殿前副都指揮使王宗濋引衛兵遁逃，致都城失守，責官、邵州安置。

translations.literal: Former Deputy Commander of the Palace Guard Wang Zongchu fled with the guard and lost the capital; he was demoted in office and settled at Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongchu of the Palace Guard had fled with the guard and lost the capital; he was demoted and sent to Shao.

sentences.zh: 徽猷閣直學士徐秉哲假資政殿學士，為大金通問使，秉哲辭。

translations.literal: Huaiyou Pavilion academician Xu Bingzhe was provisionally made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Great Jin inquiry envoy; Bingzhe declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bingzhe was offered grand academician and envoy to Great Jin; he refused.

sentences.zh: 庚申，封靖康軍節度使仲湜嗣濮王。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: Jingkang army military commissioner Zhong Shi was made heir to the Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Zhong Shi of Jingkang was made heir to the Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 粘罕還屯雲中。

translations.literal: Nianhan withdrew to camp at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan drew back to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，命新任郎官未經上殿者並引對。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: all new palace officials not yet presented were ordered to audience.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, every new palace official not yet presented was called to audience.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞顏岐罷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yan Qi was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qi left the censorate.

sentences.zh: 徐秉哲責官、梅州安置。

translations.literal: Xu Bingzhe was demoted in office and settled at Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bingzhe was demoted and sent to Mei.

sentences.zh: 詔河北、京、陝、淮、湖、江、浙州軍縣鎮募人修築城壁。

translations.literal: An edict: Hebei, Jing, Shaan, Huai, lake, river, and Zhe prefectures, counties, and posts were to recruit men to repair walls.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei, Jing, Shaan, Huai, and the lake, river, and Zhe circuits were told to recruit wall-builders.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，置登聞檢鼓院。

translations.literal: Day renxu: the Petition Drum and Petition Board office was established.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the Petition Drum court was opened.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以黃潛善為門下侍郎兼權中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Day guihai: Huang Qianshan was made Vice Director of the Chancellery concurrent acting Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Qianshan took the chancellery and acting secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌坐僭逆，責降昭化軍節度副使、潭州安置。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang was punished for usurpation, demoted to military vice commissioner of Zhaohua army and settled at Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang, guilty of usurpation, was cut to Zhaohua vice commissioner and sent to Tan.

sentences.zh: 及受偽命臣僚：王時雍高州，吳開永州，莫儔全州，李擢柳州，孫覿歸州，並安置。

translations.literal: Officials who had accepted the false mandate: Wang Shiyong to Gao, Wu Kai to Yong, Mo Chou to Quan, Li Zhuo to Liu, Sun Jue to Gui—all settled.
translations.idiomatic: Collaborators were scattered: Wang Shiyong to Gao, Wu Kai to Yong, Mo Chou to Quan, Li Zhuo to Liu, Sun Jue to Gui.

sentences.zh: 顏博文、王紹以下論罪有差。

translations.literal: Yan Bowen, Wang Shao, and those below were punished according to their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bowen, Wang Shao, and lesser men were punished to their guilt.

sentences.zh: 以知懷州霍安國、河東宣撫使劉韐死節，贈安國延康殿學士，韐資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: Huai prefecture defender Huo Anguo and Hebei-east pacification commissioner Liu Yi died loyal; Anguo was posthumously made Yankang Hall academician and Yi Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Anguo of Huai and Liu Yi of Hebei-east died loyal; Anguo was made Yankang academician, Yi grand academician, after death.

sentences.zh: 甲子，命李綱兼禦營使。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: Li Gang was ordered concurrent Imperial Camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Li Gang also took the Imperial Camp.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以龍神衛四廂都指揮使馬忠為河北經制使，措置民兵。

translations.literal: Day yichou: Dragon Spirit Guard fourth-cohort commander Ma Zhong was made Hebei pacification commissioner to arrange militia.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Ma Zhong of the Dragon Spirit Guard was made Hebei commissioner to set the militia in order.

sentences.zh: 洪芻罷左諫議大夫，下臺獄。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Commissioner Hong Chu was dismissed and sent to the censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chu left the left remonstrance and was jailed by the censors.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以祠部員外郎喻汝礪為四川撫諭，督漕計羨緡及常平錢物。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: Department of Rites Outer Office Attendant Yu Rulü was made Sichuan pacification commissioner to oversee transport surplus and Ever-Normal funds.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Yu Rulü of Rites was sent to Sichuan to oversee transport surplus and Ever-Normal grain.

sentences.zh: 罷開封、諸州、軍、府司錄曹掾官。

translations.literal: Kaifeng and all prefectural, army, and circuit recorder posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng and every circuit recorder post were struck.

sentences.zh: 州、軍通判二員者省其一。

translations.literal: Where a prefecture or army had two transit judges, one was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures with two transit judges kept one.

sentences.zh: 權減宰執奉賜三之一。

translations.literal: Chief ministers’ stipends and gifts were cut by a third.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers’ stipends were cut a third.

sentences.zh: 省諸路提舉常平司、兩浙、福建提舉市舶司。

translations.literal: Ever-Normal offices on every route and the Zhe and Fujian maritime trade offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Route Ever-Normal offices and Zhe and Fujian maritime trade bureaus were shut.

sentences.zh: 賊李孝忠寇襄陽，守臣黃叔敖棄城遁。

translations.literal: Bandit Li Xiaozhong raided Xiangyang; defender Huang Shua abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaozhong raided Xiangyang; Huang Shua fled and left the walls empty.

sentences.zh: 立格買馬。

translations.literal: A fixed schedule for buying horses was set.
translations.idiomatic: Horse purchases were put on a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以子旉生，大赦。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: because the son Huan was born, a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the birth of the son Huan brought great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 籍天下神霄宮錢谷充經費。

translations.literal: Spirit Marvel palace funds throughout the realm were registered for state use.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Marvel funds empire-wide were seized for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 拘天下職田錢隸提刑司。

translations.literal: Office-field money throughout the realm was seized for the circuit inspection offices.
translations.idiomatic: Office-field money was taken for the inspection circuits.

sentences.zh: 還元祐黨籍及上書人恩數。

translations.literal: Yuanyou faction registers and memorialists’ favors were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou faction lists and memorialists’ honors were restored.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔陝西、山東諸路帥臣團結軍民，互相應援。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: an edict—Shaanxi and Shandong route commanders were to rally troops and people for mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Shaanxi and Shandong commanders were told to rally troops and folk for mutual rescue.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，增諸縣弓手，置武尉領之。

translations.literal: Day yihai: bowmen in every county were increased; military captains were set over them.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, county bowmen were increased and military captains set over them.

sentences.zh: 宗室叔向以所募勤王兵屯京師，或言為變，命劉光世捕誅之。

translations.literal: Clansman Shuxiang camped at the capital with troops he had raised for the throne; some said he meant revolt; Liu Guangshi was ordered to seize and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Shuxiang held rescue troops at the capital; rumor said mutiny; Liu Guangshi was told to take and kill him.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以汪伯彥知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: Wang Boyan was made Director of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Boyan directed Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 遣宣義郎傅雱使河東軍前，通問二帝。

translations.literal: Promotion Attendant Fu Yun was sent to the Hedong front to inquire after the two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yun was sent to Hedong to ask after the captive emperors.

sentences.zh: 己卯，置沿河、沿淮、沿江帥府十有九，要郡三十九，次要郡三十八，帥守兼都總管，守臣兼鈐轄、都監，總置軍九十六萬七千五百人。

translations.literal: Day jimao: along the Yellow River, Huai, and Yangtze, nineteen command headquarters, thirty-nine key prefectures, and thirty-eight secondary prefectures were set; commanders were also overall commanders, defenders also seal and oversee; nine hundred sixty-seven thousand five hundred troops in all.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, nineteen river commands, thirty-nine key prefectures, and thirty-eight secondary ones were set with nine hundred sixty-seven thousand five hundred men under seal and command.

sentences.zh: 別置水軍七十七將，造舟江、淮諸路。

translations.literal: Seventy-seven water-army commands were set apart; boats were built on the Jiang and Huai routes.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-seven water commands were added and boats built on Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 置三省、樞密院賞功司。

translations.literal: The Three Departments and Military Affairs reward office was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments and Military Affairs opened a rewards office.

sentences.zh: 東京留守范訥落節鉞、淄州居住。

translations.literal: Dongjing defender Fan Nuo was stripped of command and settled at Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Nuo lost Dongjing and was sent to Zi.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以二帝未還，禁州縣用樂。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: because the two emperors had not yet returned, prefectures and counties were forbidden music.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, with the two emperors still captive, prefectures and counties were forbidden music.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，置沿河巡察六使。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: six inspectors along the river were established.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, six river patrol inspectors were appointed.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以戶部尚書張愨同知樞密院事兼提舉措置戶部財用。

translations.literal: Day renwu: Revenue Minister Zhang Chou was made associate military affairs commissioner and charged with arranging revenue ministry finances.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Revenue Minister Zhang Chou became associate military affairs commissioner and head of revenue arrangements.

sentences.zh: 癸未，呂好問罷。

translations.literal: Day guiwei: Lu Haowen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Lu Haowen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 甲申，並尚書戶部右曹所掌歸左曹，命尚書總領。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: the right section of the Revenue Ministry was merged into the left, and the minister was ordered to oversee all.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Revenue Ministry’s right section was merged into the left under the minister’s overall charge.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以宗澤為東京留守，杜充為北京留守，罷監司州郡職田。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Zong Ze was made defender of the Eastern Capital, Du Chong defender of the Northern Capital, and supervisory officials’ official-field income was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Zong Ze became Eastern Capital defender and Du Chong Northern Capital defender; supervisory officials’ official fields were abolished.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔陝西、河北、京東西路募兵合十萬人，更番入衛行在。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: an edict ordered Shaanxi, Hebei, and western capital circuits to recruit one hundred thousand men in rotation to guard the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Shaanxi, Hebei, and western capital circuits were ordered to recruit one hundred thousand men in rotation for the mobile court guard.

sentences.zh: 命京東、西路造戰車。

translations.literal: The eastern capital and western capital circuits were ordered to build war carts.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western capital circuits were ordered to build war carts.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以張所為河北西路招撫使。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: Zhang Suo was made pacification commissioner of western Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Zhang Suo was made western Hebei pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 括買官民馬，勸出財助國。

translations.literal: Official and private horses were requisitioned and the people were urged to donate to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Official and private horses were requisitioned and the people urged to donate to the state.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以錢蓋為陝西經制使，封趙懷恩為安化郡王，因召五路兵赴行在。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: Qian Gai was made Shaanxi commissioner-general; Zhao Huaien was enfeoffed Prince of Anhua commandery; and troops of the five circuits were summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Qian Gai became Shaanxi commissioner-general, Zhao Huaien was enfeoffed Prince of Anhua, and five-circuit troops were summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己丑朔，以樞密副都承旨王𤫉為河東經制使。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jichou new moon: Military Affairs deputy senior attendant Wang Qi was made Hedong commissioner-general.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, jichou new moon: Military Affairs deputy senior attendant Wang Qi became Hedong commissioner-general.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔王淵、劉光世、統制官張俊、喬仲福、韓世忠分討陳州軍賊杜用、京東賊李昱及黎驛、魚台潰兵，皆平之。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: an edict ordered Wang Yuan, Liu Guangshi, and controllers Zhang Jun, Qiao Zhongfu, and Han Shizhong each to suppress Chen prefecture army-bandit Du Yong, eastern capital bandit Li Yu, and mutineers at Li Post and Yutai—all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Wang Yuan, Liu Guangshi, and controllers Zhang Jun, Qiao Zhongfu, and Han Shizhong were sent against Chenzhou’s Du Yong, eastern capital bandit Li Yu, and mutineers at Li Post and Yutai—all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，籍東南諸州神霄宮及贍學錢助國用。

translations.literal: Day xinmao: the funds of Spirit Empyrean palaces and school endowments in southeastern circuits were registered to aid state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Spirit Empyrean palace and school endowment funds in the southeast were seized for state expenses.

sentences.zh: 叔右監門衛大將軍、貴州團練使士珸以磁、洺義兵復洺州。

translations.literal: The emperor’s younger cousin, Right Gate Guard senior general and Guizhou regiment commander Shi Yu, with Ci and Mo righteous troops recovered Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s cousin, senior Right Gate Guard general and Guizhou regiment commander Shi Yu, with Ci–Mo righteous troops recovered Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以溫州觀察使范瓊為定武軍承宣使、禦營司同都統制。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: Wenzhou observation commissioner Fan Qiong was made Dingwu Army commissioner and associate overall controller of the Imperial Escort.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Wenzhou observation commissioner Fan Qiong became Dingwu commissioner and associate Imperial Escort controller.

sentences.zh: 丙申，賜諸路強壯巡社名為「忠義巡社」，專隸安撫司。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: strong patrol companies in every circuit were given the name “Loyal and Righteous Patrol Companies” and placed solely under pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, circuit strong patrol companies were named Loyal and Righteous Patrol Companies and placed under pacification commissioners alone.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，欽宗至燕山府。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Qinzong reached Yan Mountains prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Qinzong reached Yan Mountains prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以忻州觀察使張昪為河北制置使。

translations.literal: Xinzhou observation commissioner Zhang Bian was made Hebei commissioner-general.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou observation commissioner Zhang Bian became Hebei commissioner-general.

sentences.zh: 東都宣武卒杜林謀據成都叛，伏誅。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital Xuanwu soldiers’ Du Lin plotted to seize Chengdu and rebel; he was executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital Xuanwu soldier Du Lin plotted to seize Chengdu and rebel; he was executed secretly.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔台省、寺監繁簡相兼，學官、館職減舊制之半。

translations.literal: Day jihai: an edict ordered the central ministries and directorates to share heavy and light duties, and academic and archive posts were cut to half the old establishment.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, central ministries and directorates were ordered to share heavy and light duties, and academic and archive posts were halved.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，復議吳開、莫儔等十一人罪，並廣南、江、湖諸州安置，餘遞貶有差。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: the cases of Wu Kai, Mo Chou, and eleven others were reconsidered; all were placed in the far south and in Jiang, lake, and other circuits, the rest demoted by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Wu Kai, Mo Chou, and eleven others were retried; all were exiled to the far south and Jiang–lake circuits, the rest demoted by degrees.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔：「奉元祐太后如東南，六宮及衛士家屬從行，朕當獨留中原，與金人決戰。

translations.literal: Day renyin: an edict: “Escort the Yuanyou Empress to the southeast; the six palaces and guards’ families shall follow; I alone shall remain in the central plains to give battle with the Jin.”
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, an edict: “Escort the Yuanyou Empress southeast with the six palaces and guards’ families; I alone shall remain in the central plains to fight the Jin.”

sentences.zh: 」以延康殿學士許翰為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Extended-Kang Hall academician Xu Han was made right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Extended-Kang Hall academician Xu Han became right vice director.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以右諫議大夫宋齊愈當金人謀立異姓，書張邦昌姓名，斬於都市。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: right remonstrance drafter Song Qiyu, for plotting with the Jin to enthrone another surname and writing Zhang Bangchang’s name, was beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, right remonstrance drafter Song Qiyu, who had written Zhang Bangchang’s name when the Jin plotted another ruler, was beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，手詔：「京師未可往，當巡幸東南。

translations.literal: Day yisi: a hand edict: “The capital must not yet be visited; one should tour the southeast.”
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, a hand edict: “The capital must not yet be visited; tour the southeast.”

sentences.zh: 」丙午，詔定議巡幸南陽。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: an edict fixed the tour at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, an edict fixed the imperial progress at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿學士范致虛知鄧州，修城池，繕宮室，輸錢谷以實之。

translations.literal: Literary Hall academician Fan Zhixu was made Deng prefect; he repaired walls and palaces and forwarded money and grain to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Literary Hall academician Fan Zhixu became Deng prefect, repaired walls and palaces, and forwarded money and grain to stock them.

sentences.zh: 丁未，遣官詣京師迎奉太廟神主赴行在。

translations.literal: Day dingwei: officials were sent to the capital to escort the ancestral temple spirit tablets to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, officials were sent to escort the ancestral temple tablets to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 己酉，罷四道都總管。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: the four-route overall commanders were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the four-route overall commanders were abolished.

sentences.zh: 以尚書虞部員外郎張浚為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Revenue Ministry aide Zhang Jun was made palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Ministry aide Zhang Jun became palace censor.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，征諸道兵，期八月會行在。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: troops of every circuit were levied to assemble at the mobile court in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, every circuit was levied to assemble troops at the mobile court in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，徽宗自燕山密遣閣門宣贊舍人曹勳至，賜帝絹半臂，書其領曰：「便可即真，來援父母。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: Huizong secretly sent Gate Bureau praise attendant Cao Xun from Yan Mountains with a half-sleeve silk gift for the emperor, writing on the collar: “You may at once take the true throne and come to aid your parents.”
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Huizong secretly sent Gate Bureau praise attendant Cao Xun from Yan Mountains with a half-sleeve silk for the emperor, writing on the collar: “Take the true throne at once and come to aid your parents.”

sentences.zh: 」帝泣以示輔臣。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and showed it to his chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and showed it to his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 張所、傅亮軍發行在。

translations.literal: Zhang Suo’s and Fu Liang’s armies set out from the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suo’s and Fu Liang’s armies set out from the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 是月，關中賊史斌犯興州，僭號稱帝。

translations.literal: That month Guanzhong bandit Shi Bin attacked Xing prefecture and styled himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That month Guanzhong bandit Shi Bin attacked Xing and styled himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 八月戊午朔，洪芻等坐圍城日括金銀自盜，及私納宮人，芻及餘大均、陳沖貸死，流沙門島，餘五人罪有差。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day wuwu new moon: Hong Chu and others, for extorting gold and silver during the siege and privately taking palace women, were punished—Chu and Yu Dajun and Chen Chong received commuted death and exile to Shamen Island, the other five by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, wuwu new moon: Hong Chu and others were punished for extorting gold and silver in the siege and taking palace women—Chu, Yu Dajun, and Chen Chong were commuted to exile on Shamen Island, five others by degrees.

sentences.zh: 勝捷軍校陳通作亂於杭州，執帥臣葉夢得，殺漕臣吳昉。

translations.literal: Victorious Army controller Chen Tong mutinied at Hangzhou, seized the commander Ye Mengde, and killed transport commissioner Wu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious Army controller Chen Tong mutinied at Hangzhou, seized commander Ye Mengde, and killed transport commissioner Wu Fang.

sentences.zh: 己未，元祐太后發京師。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: the Yuanyou Empress left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the Yuanyou Empress left the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以劉光世為奉國軍節度使，韓世忠、張俊皆進一官。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: Liu Guangshi was made Fengguo military commissioner; Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun each advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Liu Guangshi became Fengguo military commissioner; Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun each advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，右司諫潘良貴罷。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: right remonstrance censor Pan Lianggui was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, right remonstrance censor Pan Lianggui was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以李綱為尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，黃潛善為右僕射兼中書侍郎，張愨兼禦營副使。

translations.literal: Day renxu: Li Gang was made left vice director and gate department vice director; Huang Qianshan right vice director and secretariat vice director; Zhang Chou was also made associate Imperial Escort controller.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Li Gang became left vice director and gate vice director, Huang Qianshan right vice director and secretariat vice director, and Zhang Chou associate Imperial Escort controller.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，命禦營使、副大閱五軍。

translations.literal: Day guiha: the Imperial Escort commander and deputy were ordered to review the five armies.
translations.idiomatic: On guiha, the Imperial Escort commander and deputy were ordered to review the five armies.

sentences.zh: 庚午，更號元祐太后為隆祐太后。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: the Yuanyou Empress’s title was changed to Longyou Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Yuanyou Empress was renamed Longyou Empress.

sentences.zh: 辛未，罷傅亮經制副使，召赴行在。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: Fu Liang’s associate commissioner-general post was abolished and he was recalled to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Fu Liang’s associate commissioner post was abolished and he was recalled to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 壬申，召布衣譙定赴行在。

translations.literal: Day renshen: commoner Qiao Ding was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, commoner Qiao Ding was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 命禦營統制辛道宗討陳通。

translations.literal: Imperial Escort controller Xin Daozong was ordered to suppress Chen Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Escort controller Xin Daozong was ordered to suppress Chen Tong.

sentences.zh: 是夕，東北方有赤氣。

translations.literal: That evening there was red vapor in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: That evening red vapor appeared in the northeast.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以耿南仲主和誤國，南雄州安置。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: Geng Nanzhong, for leading peace talks and ruining the state, was placed at Nanxiong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Geng Nanzhong was exiled to Nanxiong for leading peace talks and ruining the state.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，用張浚言，罷李綱左僕射。

translations.literal: Day yihai: on Zhang Jun’s advice, Li Gang was dismissed as left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, on Zhang Jun’s advice, Li Gang was dismissed as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 丙子，隆祐太后發南京，命侍衛馬軍都指揮使郭仲荀護衛如江甯，兼節制江、淮、荊、浙、閩、廣諸州，制置東南盜賊。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: the Longyou Empress left the Southern Capital; Palace Attendant Horse Army commander Guo Zhongxun was ordered to escort her to Jiangning and also to command Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and Guang circuits and to arrange southeastern bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Longyou Empress left the Southern Capital; Horse Army commander Guo Zhongxun escorted her to Jiangning and commanded Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and Guang while arranging southeastern bandits.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以龍圖閣直學士錢伯言知杭州，節制兩浙、淮東將兵及福建槍杖手，討陳通。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: Dragon Diagram Hall academician Qian Boyan was made Hangzhou prefect, commanding the two Zhe and Huai-east armies and Fujian pike troops to suppress Chen Tong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Dragon Diagram Hall academician Qian Boyan became Hangzhou prefect, commanding Zhe and Huai-east troops and Fujian pikes against Chen Tong.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，降榜招諭杭州亂兵。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: a placard of amnesty was issued to win over Hangzhou mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, an amnesty placard was issued to win over Hangzhou mutineers.

sentences.zh: 壬午，用黃潛善議，殺上書太學生陳東、崇仁布衣歐陽澈。

translations.literal: Day renwu: on Huang Qianshan’s advice, the memorializing university student Chen Dong and Chongren commoner Ouyang Che were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, on Huang Qianshan’s advice, memorializing student Chen Dong and Chongren commoner Ouyang Che were executed.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，遣兵部員外郎江端友等撫諭閩、浙、湖、廣、江、淮、京東西諸路，及體訪官吏貪廉、軍民利病。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Revenue Ministry aide Jiang Duanyou and others were sent to reassure Fujian, Zhe, lake, Guang, Jiang, Huai, and eastern and western capital circuits and to investigate officials’ greed and integrity and army–people hardships.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Revenue aide Jiang Duanyou and others were sent to reassure Fujian, Zhe, lake, Guang, Jiang, Huai, and capital circuits and to investigate officials and popular hardship.

sentences.zh: 許翰罷。

translations.literal: Xu Han was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Han was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，博州卒宮儀作亂，犯萊州。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: Bozhou soldiers under Gong Yi mutinied and attacked Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Bozhou soldiers under Gong Yi mutinied and attacked Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，建州軍校張員等作亂，執守臣張動，轉運副使毛奎、判官曹仔為所殺，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Jianzhou soldiers under Zhang Yuan and others mutinied, seized defender Zhang Dong, and killed transport vice commissioner Mao Kui and judge Cao Zai; they held the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, jichou: Jianzhou soldiers under Zhang Yuan mutinied, seized Zhang Dong, killed Mao Kui and Cao Zai, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 范瓊捕斬李孝忠於復州。

translations.literal: Fan Qiong captured and beheaded Li Xiaozhong at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiong captured and beheaded Li Xiaozhong at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以金人犯河陽、汜水，詔擇日巡幸淮甸。

translations.literal: Day renchen: because the Jin attacked Heyang and Sishui, an edict chose a day to tour the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, with Jin attacking Heyang and Sishui, an edict chose a day to tour the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 鑄建炎通寶錢。

translations.literal: Jianyan universal treasure cash was cast.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan universal treasure cash was cast.

sentences.zh: 命淮、浙沿海諸州增修城壁，招訓民兵，以備海道。

translations.literal: Coastal prefectures of Huai and Zhe were ordered to heighten walls, recruit and train militia, and prepare the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and Zhe coastal prefectures were ordered to heighten walls, train militia, and guard the sea routes.

sentences.zh: 甲午，命揚州守臣呂頤浩繕修城池。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: Yangzhou defender Lü Yihao was ordered to repair walls.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Yangzhou defender Lü Yihao was ordered to repair the walls.

sentences.zh: 宗澤往河北視師，七日還。

translations.literal: Zong Ze went to Hebei to inspect the armies and returned in seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze went to Hebei to inspect the armies and returned in seven days.

sentences.zh: 是夜，辛道宗兵潰於嘉興縣。

translations.literal: That night Xin Daozong’s troops collapsed at Jiaxing county.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xin Daozong’s troops collapsed at Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔荊襄、關陝、江淮皆備巡幸。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: an edict ordered Jing–Xiang, Guan–Shaan, and Jiang–Huai all to prepare for the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Jing–Xiang, Guan–Shaan, and Jiang–Huai were ordered to prepare for the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，罷買馬。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: horse purchases were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, horse purchases were abolished.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以子旉為檢校少保、集慶軍節度使，封魏國公。

translations.literal: Day jihai: the son Fang was made acting Junior Guardian and Jiqing military commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the son Fang was made acting Junior Guardian and Jiqing military commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔內外官司參用嘉祐、元豐敕，以俟新書。

translations.literal: An edict ordered inner and outer offices to apply provisionally the Jiayou and Yuanfeng statutes pending new books.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer offices were ordered to apply Jiayou and Yuanfeng statutes provisionally pending new codes.

sentences.zh: 庚子，二帝徙居霫郡。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: the two emperors were moved to Xi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the two emperors were moved to Xi commandery.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，陳通劫提點刑獄周格營，殺格，執提點刑獄高士曈。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: Chen Tong raided judicial intendant Zhou Ge’s camp, killed Ge, and seized judicial intendant Gao Shitan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Chen Tong raided judicial intendant Zhou Ge’s camp, killed Ge, and seized Gao Shitan.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，遣徽猷閣待制孟忠厚迎奉太廟神主赴揚州。

translations.literal: Day renyin: Imperial Writings Hall attendant Meng Zhonghou was sent to escort the ancestral temple tablets to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Imperial Writings attendant Meng Zhonghou was sent to escort the ancestral tablets to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣王圭為招撫判官，代張所，尋責所廣南安置。

translations.literal: Direct Secretariat academician Wang Gui was made pacification judge, replacing Zhang Suo; soon Suo was blamed and placed in the far south.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Secretariat academician Wang Gui replaced Zhang Suo as pacification judge; soon Suo was exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，宗澤表請車駕還闕。

translations.literal: Day yisi: Zong Ze memorialized asking the imperial carriage to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Zong Ze memorialized asking the throne to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊申，河北招撫司都統制王彥渡河擊金人，破之，復新鄉縣。

translations.literal: Day wushen: Hebei pacification headquarters overall controller Wang Yan crossed the river, defeated the Jin, and recovered Xinxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Hebei pacification overall controller Wang Yan crossed the river, defeated the Jin, and recovered Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以諜報金人欲犯江、浙，詔暫駐淮甸捍禦，稍定即還京闕。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: on intelligence that the Jin meant to attack Jiang and Zhe, an edict ordered a temporary halt in the Huai region for defense and return to the capital once settled.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, hearing the Jin meant to attack Jiang and Zhe, an edict halted temporarily in the Huai region for defense and promised return to the capital once settled.

sentences.zh: 募民入貲授官。

translations.literal: The people were recruited to buy office with wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were recruited to buy office with wealth.

sentences.zh: 軍賊趙萬入常州，執守臣何袞。

translations.literal: Army-bandit Zhao Wan entered Changzhou and seized defender He Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Army-bandit Zhao Wan entered Changzhou and seized defender He Gun.

sentences.zh: 罷諸路經制招撫使。

translations.literal: Circuit commissioner-generals and pacification commissioners were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioner-generals and pacification commissioners were abolished.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，始通當三大錢於淮、浙、荊湖諸路。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: the three-large cash was first circulated in Huai, Zhe, and Jing–lake circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the three-large cash was first circulated in Huai, Zhe, and Jing–lake circuits.

sentences.zh: 壬子，命湖南撫諭官馬伸持詔賜張邦昌死於潭州，並誅王時雍。

translations.literal: Day renzi: Hunan reassurance commissioner Ma Shen was ordered to carry an edict granting Zhang Bangchang death at Tanzhou and also to execute Wang Shiyong.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Hunan reassurance commissioner Ma Shen was ordered to grant Zhang Bangchang death at Tanzhou and execute Wang Shiyong.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔有敢妄議惑眾沮巡幸者，許告而罪之，不告者斬。

translations.literal: Day guichou: an edict—whoever rashly debated and misled the masses to obstruct the progress might be reported and punished; those who did not report were to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, whoever rashly debated to obstruct the progress might be reported and punished; non-reporters were to be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，王彥及金人戰，敗績，奔太行山聚眾，其裨將岳飛引其部曲自為一軍。

translations.literal: Day yimao: Wang Yan fought the Jin and was defeated; he fled to the Taihang Mountains to gather troops; his lieutenant Yue Fei led his own detachment as a separate army.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Wang Yan fought the Jin, was defeated, fled to the Taihang to gather troops; lieutenant Yue Fei led his detachment separately.

sentences.zh: 趙萬陷鎮江府，守臣趙子崧棄城渡江，保瓜洲。

translations.literal: Zhao Wan took Zhenjiang prefecture; defender Zhao Zisong abandoned the city, crossed the river, and held Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wan took Zhenjiang; Zhao Zisong abandoned the city, crossed the river, and held Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 是秋，金人分兵據兩河州縣，惟中山、慶源府、保、莫、邢洺、冀、磁、絳、相州久之乃陷。
